entries.definition: The endpoint on the application side that receives the signed SAML response posted by Okta; when the URL entered in the app integration differs from what the app expects, users see a sign-in error instead of the app.

Microsoft's on-premises Windows directory of users, groups and computers; Okta connects to it through a lightweight agent to import accounts, delegate password checks and push changes back to domain objects.
A programmatic interface that lets scripts and tools read or change org objects such as users, groups and apps; admins create tokens for it under Security and limit them by the role of the creator.

Okta's earlier product for brokering short-lived certificate-based SSH and RDP logins to Linux and Windows servers without static keys; its capabilities have since been folded into Okta Privileged Access.

Identifier assigned to an internet routing domain, typically one ISP or hosting provider; dynamic network zones can match or block requests by this value to deny traffic from whole carrier or cloud networks.
The US Department of Defense smart card carrying the holder's certificates; Okta can accept it through the smart card authenticator so personnel sign in by inserting the card and entering its PIN.
Notation such as 203.0.113.0/24 that writes an address range as a base address plus prefix length; admins use it to list office or proxy ranges when defining IP network zones.
A text-based tool run in a terminal; developers and admins use Okta's version, or Terraform, to script tasks such as registering OIDC app integrations instead of clicking through the Admin Console.

Browser mechanism that decides whether JavaScript from one website may call an API on another; admins add trusted origins under Security so single-page apps can call Okta endpoints directly from the browser.
Shorthand for the four basic data operations; custom admin roles are built by granting a subset of them, for example letting helpdesk staff view and edit users without being able to remove them.
Plain-text tabular file format with one record per line; admins use it to bulk-import users with their attributes and to download report and System Log results for offline review.
The full path that uniquely locates an entry in an LDAP or Active Directory tree, such as CN=Ana,OU=Sales,DC=corp,DC=com; directory integrations use it to pick which containers to import from.

Feature that signs domain-joined Windows users into Okta silently using their Kerberos ticket from logging onto the PC; the agentless version is configured with a service account and an identity provider routing rule.

Security software on laptops and desktops that monitors processes for attacks; Okta Verify can read its health signals so authentication policies allow access only from devices the tool reports as healthy.

Open passwordless standard pairing WebAuthn with hardware security keys or platform biometrics such as Touch ID and Windows Hello; it resists phishing because keys are bound to the real site's origin.
A JSON file recorded from browser developer tools that captures every request and response in a session; Okta Support often asks for one to trace redirect loops or failed federation exchanges.

The system of record for employees, such as Workday or BambooHR; when set as a profile source, it drives creation, attribute updates and deactivation of Okta accounts from hiring and termination events.

The request-response protocol browsers and APIs use; its status codes, like 401 for missing credentials, 403 for forbidden and 429 for rate limiting, help admins diagnose failed sign-ins and integration errors.

The discipline of establishing who each person or service is and controlling what they may reach; Okta is a cloud platform for this, combining directory, sign-on, authentication and lifecycle features.

The party that verifies a user and issues assertions or tokens other apps trust; Okta usually plays this role for downstream apps, but can also hand off authentication to an external one through routing rules.
Category of tooling that controls who should hold which access through request workflows, periodic certification campaigns and audit reporting; Okta sells a dedicated add-on for this work.
The network-layer protocol that addresses and routes packets; the source address of each request appears in the System Log and is what network zones and policy rules evaluate.

Okta product that scans connected identity systems and SaaS apps for risky configurations, such as accounts lacking MFA, stale admins or unused privileged credentials, and ranks findings for remediation.
Okta capability that keeps evaluating risk after sign-in, using signals such as session hijack indicators and partner security events, and can end sessions or demand reauthentication when risk rises.
Microsoft's Kerberos or NTLM based silent sign-in for domain-joined machines; in Okta it underpins the older on-premises web agent version of desktop single sign-on running on IIS.
Provisioning style where an account is created or updated at the moment someone first signs in, using attributes from the directory or inbound assertion, rather than in advance by a scheduled import.
Shorthand for the three lifecycle events of a worker: being hired, changing role, and departing; admins automate each with group rules, app assignments and deprovisioning so access tracks the job.
Lightweight text format of key-value pairs and arrays; Okta APIs, System Log events, user profiles and token payloads are all expressed in it, so admins read it when inspecting events in detail.
A published document listing the public keys an authorization server signs tokens with; apps fetch it from the keys endpoint to verify signatures and pick up keys automatically after rotation.
Compact signed token of a header, claims payload and signature separated by dots; Okta issues ID and access tokens in this form, and apps verify the signature before trusting the claims.
Okta's automated creation, update, deactivation and reactivation of accounts in downstream apps, driven by assignments and profile changes so access appears on day one and disappears at departure.
Open protocol for querying and modifying directory entries; Okta's agent for it imports users from servers like OpenLDAP, and Okta can also expose an interface of this kind for legacy apps.

Tools that enroll and control phones and tablets, enforcing passcodes, encryption and app deployment; Okta device assurance and policies can require a device to be managed by such a tool before granting access.
Requiring proof from two or more categories, such as something you know, have or are, before access; Okta enforces it through authenticator enrollment rules and authentication policy settings.
Identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 that adds an ID token describing the signed-in user; it is the usual protocol for modern web, mobile and single-page app integrations created in Okta.
The current Okta platform generation, replacing Classic Engine, that introduced app-level authentication policies, flexible authenticator choices, passwordless options and customizable sign-in flows.
Okta's add-on product for access requests, certification campaigns and entitlement management, used to prove periodically that each person's app and group access is still appropriate.
Okta's catalog of thousands of prebuilt connectors for third-party applications; admins browse it to add an app with preconfigured sign-on and, where supported, provisioning settings.
Okta product that vaults shared credentials and brokers just-in-time, audited access to servers and privileged accounts, replacing standing admin passwords with approved, time-limited sessions.
A short code valid for a single use, delivered by email, text, voice call or generated by an app; Okta authenticators use it as a possession factor during sign-in or account recovery.
Container inside Active Directory or LDAP that groups users, groups and computers; admins choose which ones Okta imports from and which one receives users created through provisioning.

Discipline and tooling for securing high-risk accounts such as administrators and service credentials through vaulting, session control and just-in-time elevation; Okta sells a dedicated product for this work.
Base64 text encoding of certificates and keys wrapped in BEGIN and END lines; admins download Okta's SAML signing certificate in this form to upload into service provider settings.
US federal civilian smart card standard (FIPS 201) holding certificates for employees and contractors; Okta's smart card authenticator can accept these cards as a phishing-resistant sign-in method.

OAuth extension in which the client sends a hashed random secret with the authorization request and the original at the token step, stopping intercepted codes from being redeemed; required for Okta native and single-page apps.

The system of certificate authorities, certificates and revocation lists that binds public keys to identities; Okta relies on it for smart card sign-in, device certificates and signed federation messages.
Older network authentication protocol used by VPNs and Wi-Fi gear; the Okta agent for it lets those devices check credentials and prompt for Okta Verify push or codes as a second factor.
Granting permissions through named roles rather than to individuals; Okta applies it to administration with standard roles like Super Administrator and custom roles scoped to resource sets.
Architectural style for web APIs using resource URLs and standard verbs like GET, POST and DELETE; Okta's management and System Log APIs follow it and return JSON.
XML-based federation standard in which Okta sends a signed assertion about the user to an application; admins configure audience URI, endpoint URL, name ID format and attribute statements.
Standard REST schema and protocol for creating, updating and deactivating user and group records in remote apps; Okta uses it to push provisioning changes to supporting applications.
Packaged libraries, samples and documentation for a language or platform; developers use Okta's versions to embed sign-in, validate tokens or call management APIs without writing raw HTTP calls.

Family of cryptographic digest functions; the 256-bit second-generation variant is Okta's default for signing SAML assertions, while some older service providers still expect the weaker 160-bit first version.
Platform such as Splunk or Microsoft Sentinel that collects and correlates logs from many sources; admins stream Okta System Log events to it for alerting, long-term retention and investigations.
SAML feature in which ending a session in one place sends logout messages so the identity provider and participating apps all end their sessions; it needs a logout URL and signing certificate.
Mobile text messaging; Okta's phone authenticator can send codes this way, but because of SIM swapping and interception it is considered weak and often limited to recovery only.
Tooling that runs playbooks to triage alerts and act on them automatically; it can consume Okta events and call Okta APIs to suspend users or clear sessions during an incident.
Control that prevents one person from holding conflicting powers, such as requesting and approving the same access; Okta governance and custom roles can be designed to enforce it.
The application side of a federation that trusts assertions from an identity provider; admins enter its entity ID and endpoint details in the Okta app integration.
Signing in once and then reaching many applications without retyping credentials; Okta delivers it through SAML, OIDC and password-vaulting integrations launched from the End-User Dashboard.

Lets users regain access after forgetting a password by proving identity with an enrolled authenticator such as email or Okta Verify, configured in the password policy's recovery settings to reduce helpdesk calls.
Okta's password-vaulting sign-on method for apps without federation support: Okta stores encrypted credentials and the browser plugin fills and submits the app's own login form.
Protocol that encrypts and authenticates network connections, the basis of HTTPS; Okta requires it for all traffic, for custom domain certificates and for secure directory agent connections.
Algorithm (RFC 6238) generating six-digit codes from a shared secret and the current time, rotating every 30 seconds; Okta Verify and Google Authenticator produce codes this way.
Earlier FIDO standard for hardware keys used as an additional factor after a password; it was superseded by FIDO2, which Okta supports through its security key or biometric authenticator.
Okta's cloud user store that holds profiles from many sources, supports custom attributes and maps them between Okta and apps through the Profile Editor.
Tooling that manages laptops, desktops and mobile devices from one console, such as Intune or Jamf; Okta checks whether a device is managed by it as a condition in authentication policies.
Active Directory sign-in name in email-like form such as ana@corp.com; admins often map it to the Okta username and to app usernames during directory integration.
Generic string that identifies a resource, of which web addresses are a subset; Okta uses such identifiers for SAML audience and entity IDs and for OIDC redirect and sign-out targets.
A web address giving scheme, host and path; admins enter them for app sign-on endpoints and redirect targets, and a mistyped one is a frequent cause of failed app launches.

Encrypted tunnel connecting a remote device to an internal corporate network across the internet; Okta can secure it through RADIUS or SAML, and network zones may treat traffic from known gateways as trusted.

Approach that grants access to specific applications only after verifying user identity and device posture for each request, instead of trusting anyone inside a network perimeter; Okta supplies the identity signals.
